approach.method_basis: The Parent starts at the best supplied scored molecule and repeatedly samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits from that one current graph. It sanitizes and normalizes each edited molecular identity, rejects previously proposed molecules, and submits the first full batch admitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. Memory vetoes a neighbor only when both inverse signs match the same earlier selected transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score worsens, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Bounded inverse restrictions, four-step aging, overlap refresh and obstruction release remain part of that Parent, as does the repaired proposal-to-feedback identity join.
approach.novelty: Add one local sulfur-valence introduction gate. A generated neighbor may retain or remove a sulfur environment already present in its source, but it may not introduce or multiply a sulfur environment outside an explicit small envelope of ordinary valence patterns. This redirects eligible graph edits toward alternative neighbors before they reach the unchanged memory gate. It preserves thiol and sulfide valence, aromatic sulfur, terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds, and the usual neutral sulfur-oxide patterns. Earlier siblings changed memory matching and repaired identity bookkeeping; they did not constrain sulfur chemistry. The related corpus-support experiment in another walk admitted chemistry merely because it occurred locally in a corpus. This proposal instead tests a fixed, narrow sulfur rule without learning a vocabulary or changing preparation.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 has a complete three-seed macro mean of 0.5209178281192797 and standard deviation 0.004890242222897396, and its saved summaries and run logs show successful full panels. The supplied molecular assessments repeatedly describe multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and sulfur-rich cages. Its graph kernel permits sulfur up to valence six and accepts edited graphs after sanitization without distinguishing ordinary sulfur valence patterns. An offline examination of all fifteen Parent task logs using the fixed sulfur envelope specified below finds 5285 edit attempts, 4544 valid novel draws, and 4350 emissions. Of the valid novel draws, 967 introduce or increase a disallowed sulfur-environment signature; 942 of the emitted neighbors do so, and 2398 emitted molecules contain at least one such sulfur center. All fifteen sessions have positive introduction counts. Only 462 of all 4350 accepted neighbors beat their generating source. The 213 source-beating molecules among the 2398 sulfur-violating outputs show that these patterns can receive useful scalar feedback; the descriptive groups are confounded by trajectory and do not establish that filtering improves score. The bottleneck is an exercised, chemically permissive proposal channel after successful identity recovery, rather than failed feedback or inactive memory.
hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel graph neighbor before tabu testing exactly when it introduces or increases the multiplicity of a sulfur local-environment signature outside a fixed neutral sulfur-valence envelope relative to the same scored source graph, then continue the inherited graph-edit sampling loop from that unchanged source.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate eliminated targeted violations, with higher sampling cost and uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 766 of 5,307 otherwise valid novel neighbors across all fifteen task sessions. Of those rejections, 760 would have passed the unchanged tabu rule, and every rejection was followed by a different permitted neighbor from the same scored source. None of the 4,350 emitted molecules contains sulfur outside the declared envelope, compared with 2,398 of 4,350 Parent emissions. Sulfur remains in 2,821 emitted molecules, including thiols, sulfides, aromatic sulfur, thiones, sulfoxides and sulfones.

All three seeds complete all five 300-evaluation tasks and all 435 ten-member batches. The sampling cost rises from 5,285 to 6,234 raw attempts, or 12.15 to 14.33 attempts per batch. Emission yield falls from 82.31% to 69.78% of raw attempts. Recorded edits, normalized identities, accepted-score joins and downstream memory/winner rules pass the independent audit.

Mean macro final Top-1 rises from 0.520918 to 0.526783, a paired mean change of +0.005865. The seed changes are +0.015565, -0.061423 and +0.063454, and the macro population standard deviation rises from 0.004890 to 0.046774. Zaleplon and median_2 improve in every matched seed; decoration hopping declines in every seed, while DRD2 and sitagliptin have mixed outcomes. The gate therefore achieves its intended chemical and allocation changes with an uneven score response.

molecular.headline: More conventional sulfur and amine skeletons coexist with N-halogen bonds, hypobromites and severely strained cages
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, compared with the supplied three-seed Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9379 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These are string-presence counters, not atom fractions or measurements of ionization and stereochemical feasibility. The prominent high-scoring sulfur motifs now include thiols, sulfides, thiones, sulfoxides and aromatic sulfur, rather than the Parent's frequently multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur cages. Some aromatic amine leaders are entirely sulfur-free and have substantially more recognizable medicinal skeletons. This is a real difference in the observed chemistry, but the output still includes reactive N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and O-Br bonds, N-N/N-O networks, highly constrained small rings and dense carbon/nitrogen cages. Aromatic ring/carbonyl families, large decorated diones and polycyclic amines give moderate diversity across tasks and seeds; local families dominate each late trajectory. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor because several of the leading complete structures are severely strained or reactive, despite more plausible subseries. No activation or causal attribution is inferred from these molecular observations.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic/fused-ring carbonyl compounds remain prominent. Seed 2 reaches a methoxy- and methyl-substituted indene linked to pyridine through a carbonyl-S-N unit carrying N-Br. Seed 1 contains more conventional indene aryl ketones with ethylthio, methylamino and methoxy substituents; other high examples carry hydrazine, bromomethoxy or sulfenamide groups. Seed 0 reaches an N-bromothioamide on an oxygen-containing unsaturated fused framework. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9977 and halogen presence is 0.8402. These replace the Parent's unusual-sulfur ketones or N-chloroamides with different sulfur chemistry, but several leaders still combine reactive functionalities. The aryl ketone subseries is comparatively plausible.
liabilities: Acyl-S-N-Br, N-bromothioamide and bromomethoxy groups introduce substantial reactivity despite ordinary sulfur valence.
N-N/N-O networks and constrained unsaturated ring closures remain chemically or geometrically questionable.
missing_features: Broader stable realizations of the compact aryl-carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, sulfenamide and hydrazine substitutions.

Accessible alternatives to the late bridged N-O frameworks and explicit configurations for products that acquire stereocentres are absent from the shown high/final series; no unique target-specific group is established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The carbonyl-S-N-Br compound reaches 0.4373696743346135 versus the Parent seed-2 maximum of 0.41003927643747895. A more conventional aryl ketone reaches 0.4156437178531234, and its chlorine/bromine aryl variants tie at that score, so reactive acyl-S-N-Br chemistry is not needed to approach this observed region. A ring-expanded N-containing ketone scores 0.02222493282960762, while a disrupted fused-ring thioamide scores 0.035101269092179636. Compact aromatic/carbonyl placement appears favorable relative to those expanded or disrupted structures. The final nitrogen/oxygen-rich bridged products lie below the earlier maximum.

per_task.generated_character: Large, heavily decorated nitrogen-rich diones dominate. The seed-2 best family joins the fused dione to a pyridine-like ring carrying a very small oxygen bridge, with amino-substituted linkers, brominated alkyl/alkene groups and an O-Br hypobromite. Seed 0 forms more extensively fused aromatic diones with ester/thioester and imine substituents; seed 1 reaches expanded nitrogen rings containing alkynes, imines, N-Br and halogenated side chains. Every proposal contains aromatic and ring-closure tokens, while cumulated-double-bond presence is 0.0851. Relative to the Parent's large sulfur-rich decorated cores, these products remain bulky and highly functionalized, with reactivity and ring-strain problems extending beyond sulfur valence.
liabilities: Hypobromite O-Br, N-Br, haloalkyl and imine functionality creates potential instability and reactive combinations.
Small aromatic-associated oxygen bridges, cyclic alkynes or cumulated unsaturation, and unspecified amino-linker configurations undermine whole-molecule synthetic plausibility.
missing_features: Compact, stable substituent sets around the recurring fused-dione arrangement are poorly represented among late molecules.
Accessible heteroaryl attachments without the small strained oxygen bridge, O-Br or N-halogen chemistry are missing from much of the high-scoring family.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; a modified low optimizer example scores 0.5286081645773063. The best seed-2 family reaches 0.5988528191359531, below its Parent seed-2 counterpart at 0.6092182584436399. Many alkyl, bromo/chloro and alkene variants share exactly 0.5988528191359531, as do final carbonyl/thione variants. Opening the fused dione into the final amino-containing cyclic carbonyl structure gives 0.5520804780439669. The recurring heterocyclic arrangement appears more consequential than several peripheral decorations; the plateau does not establish that the reactive groups are useful.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leaders are sulfur-free aromatic polyamines: chlorophenyl and pyridyl groups connect to an azetidine-containing polycyclic diamine framework, sometimes with aminomethyl or hydroxymethyl substituents. Related members insert an ether bridge or open part of the polycyclic framework. Seed 0 reaches more flexible aromatic tertiary-amine/sulfenamide chains, whereas seed 1 retains a sulfur heteroaromatic, amine and aryl family. Aromatic presence is 1.0 and halogen presence is 0.9954. Compared with the Parent's multiply bonded sulfur frameworks, the strongest current seed has more conventional C/N/O connectivity and recognizable medicinal architecture. Small fused rings and unspecified configurations still leave synthetic and conformational uncertainty; neutral SMILES do not establish actual protonation.
liabilities: Fused azetidine-containing frameworks have constrained geometry and unspecified ring-junction stereochemistry.
Multiple amines and aromatic groups leave ionization and physicochemical properties unresolved; other seeds still contain reactive N-S linkages or strained unsaturation.
missing_features: Accessible variants of the favorable aromatic/polyamine arrangement with less crowded small-ring fusion are underrepresented despite a high-scoring less connected analogue.
Explicit stereochemical and protonation alternatives are absent from the observed comparisons; a single required halogen or terminal polar group is not supported by the near-saturated series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 polyamine maximum is 0.999998887350651, compared with 0.9148143511682032 for the paired Parent. Early acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives remain low, including 0.007468397818197266. Many different aromatic substituents, ether insertion and a less connected ring analogue retain nearly saturated scores; the latter scores 0.9999895780003252. Opening an aromatic ring into an expanded unsaturated ring lowers the final example to 0.39449574864596665. The visible gradient supports aromatic/amine spacing while leaving substantial freedom in halogens and ring connectivity. The improvement is not uniform across seeds: the current seed-1 maximum is below its Parent counterpart.

per_task.generated_character: The highest seed-0 molecules combine ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings and a pendant alkylphenyl group with a constrained lactam/hydrazide and an oxygen-rich macrocyclic bridge. N-N and N-O connectivity is prominent. Other seeds explore related aryl lactam/ester frameworks, and the final seed-2 family adds a dense N-N-rich bridge system and N-Cl. Aromatic and ring-closure presence rates are 1.0, while halogen presence is 0.0977. Relative to the Parent's sulfur-rich bridges and brominated alternatives, these leaders mainly use C/N/O frameworks, but controlled ring closure, heteroatom compatibility and stereochemistry remain unresolved. The size is moderate to bulky, with recognizable aromatic/carbonyl fragments embedded in unusual complete structures.
liabilities: Hydrazide, N-O and acetal-like linkages complicate stability and synthetic compatibility in the macrocyclic framework.
Late dense nitrogen bridges and N-Cl combine unresolved ring geometry with reactive functionality.
missing_features: Accessible macrocyclic or fused alternatives preserving the aromatic/lactam arrangement without extensive N-N/N-O connectivity are underexplored.
Simpler stable linkers and defined configurations are absent from much of the late bridged output; the score differences do not reveal a uniquely missing target fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aromatic/lactam macrocyclic member scores 0.22352659924261728 compared with the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.2107445781802027. An opened dicarbonyl derivative scores 0.1263981386214515, and a polyene replacing aromatic structure scores 0.14644884303054695. The gradient therefore favors the retained aromatic/carbonyl arrangement in these series. Phenol and thiol substitutions tie at 0.21874182349972615, showing limited discrimination of that chemical change. The late N-chloro bridged family remains lower, including 0.19903147130554083; adding reactive nitrogen and more bridges is not consistently rewarded.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leaders remain highly compact polycyclic cages, now built from carbon/nitrogen frameworks with sulfoxide, thiol and a very small aromatic N/S ring. They contain multiple carbon-bound fluorines, an N-F cyclic carbonyl/amidine region and, in the best molecule, a severely constrained cyclic allene. Other high members replace the allene with densely fused small carbon rings. Seeds 0 and 1 also retain complex cages with sulfoxide or related oxygenated sulfur and thiol groups. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9379, higher than the broadly nonaromatic Parent cage families, but the aromatic portion is small relative to the total cage. Ordinary sulfur bonding has not made these complete structures synthetically plausible.
liabilities: A small-ring cyclic allene, very small aromatic N/S ring and densely fused cage junctions impose severe geometric and stability concerns.
N-F and thiol functionality remain reactive liabilities, and neither carbon-centre nor sulfoxide stereochemistry is specified.
missing_features: Stable accessible frameworks preserving the favorable carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorinated arrangement without the cyclic allene and densely fused small rings are not demonstrated.
Chemically conventional substitutes for the N-F motif and explicit stereochemistry at cage junctions and sulfoxide centres are absent from the shown high-scoring comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 maximum reaches 0.6534580802597463 versus its Parent maximum of 0.4484554129767839; the other paired seeds have lower maxima than their Parents. An early modified fused dione scores 7.590554525032884e-10. In a close high-scoring cage pair, replacing N-F by NH lowers 0.619441659867296 to 0.12291544159228127. Expanding the adjacent carbonyl-containing ring gives 0.12275001618495877. Thus local nitrogen substitution and ring geometry receive strong score discrimination, including a preference for a reactive N-F bond in this pair. These observations do not establish an accessible pharmacophore or reward for chemical stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Current digest leaders contain acyl-S-N-Br, N-bromothioamide, O-Br hypobromite and N-F motifs. A matched N-F versus NH cage pair scores 0.619441659867296 and 0.12291544159228127, so the observed scalar feedback can favor a chemically reactive substitution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still emits reactive nitrogen-halogen and oxygen-halogen bonds within high-scoring molecular families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable nitrogen and oxygen bonding alternatives available while preserving local attachment geometry, and represent functional-group compatibility independently of the scalar objective. Ordinary sulfur valence alone does not address these remaining liabilities.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring outputs now include a small-ring cyclic allene, a very small aromatic N/S ring, strained oxygen bridges and dense fused carbon/nitrogen cages. Other high outputs contain recognizable azetidine-containing polyamines, so small rings are not uniformly implausible.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can exchange unusual sulfur chemistry for equally problematic carbon, nitrogen and oxygen ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish accessible small rings from severely constrained multiple bonds and incompatible fused-ring closures. Provide simpler fused, spiro or ring-opened alternatives that preserve useful substituent spacing rather than treating all valid graph closures as equally feasible.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 in every current digest despite substituted polycyclic diamines, fluorinated cage junctions and unsymmetrically substituted sulfoxides. The supplied high/final structures do not compare explicitly assigned stereoisomers.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator continues to omit stereochemical specification at saturated ring junctions and stereogenic sulfur centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support consistent configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation for eligible carbon and sulfur centres, and retain that identity through generation. Any scoring benefit must be measured because these trajectories do not establish stereochemical sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A less connected aromatic polyamine analogue scores 0.9999895780003252 while more constrained relatives have nearly saturated scores. A decorated dione family shares 0.5988528191359531 across numerous side-chain and carbonyl/thione changes, and recognizable aryl ketones reach 0.4156437178531234 near more reactive alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable simpler analogues remain underexplored when a family already has broad tolerance to peripheral changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate compact linkers, fewer ring connections and stable substituent replacements around recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. This would expose accessible alternatives within the observed favorable regions without relying mainly on additional heteroatoms or complex ring closures.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
